A.topic: #45 How much should you really spend on a pram?

ig.text:
Spending more on a pram doesn't always get you more pram.
Sometimes you're paying for a colour. Sometimes it's the same model at a dearer shop. And some mid-range prices don't even include the carrycot.
👉 Swipe for what each price step really buys, plus 3 questions that set your budget.
📌 Save it before your first shop visit.

pin.text: A budget travel system can still include the carrycot and car seat. Many mid-range prices are for the pushchair alone, so check what's included before you compare. Premium prams pay off when they grow with your family. And the same pram can cost far less at another UK shop or in another colour. Compare pram prices from UK shops at BabySorted.

th.text:
How much should you really spend on a pram? What we see when we compare UK shops:
1. A full travel system with carrycot and car seat is possible on a small budget.
2. Many mid-range prices are for the pushchair only. Check what's in the box.
3. Premium prams often convert to a double, so you buy once.
4. The same pram can cost much less at another shop, or in another colour.

C.topic: #47 Winter car seat safety: the puffy coat rule

ig.text:
That cosy snowsuit could be making the car seat less safe.
Padding stops the harness sitting close to your baby's body, so it feels tight when it isn't. The fix is quick, and your baby still stays warm.
👉 Swipe for 7 checks before every cold drive, including the pinch test.
📌 Save it for the first frosty morning.
🔗 Compare car seat prices from UK shops: link in bio.
#carseatsafetyuk #ukmums #newparentsuk #pregnancyuk #winterbabyuk

pin.text: Thick coats and snowsuits stop the harness sitting close to your baby. Take them off before you strap in, check only one or two fingers fit under the harness, do the pinch test at the shoulder, lay a blanket over the top, never under, and take hats off in a warm car. Compare car seat prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Sources: RoSPA, the UK accident prevention charity, NHS and The Lullaby Trust, the UK safer baby sleep charity.

pinterestData.pinTitle: Winter Car Seat Safety: The Puffy Coat Rule (UK)

descendants.text: How to choose a car seat for a newborn in the UK https://babysorted.com/article?slug=car-seat-for-a-newborn-uk

th.text:
The puffy coat rule for car seats:
1. Coat or snowsuit off before the harness goes on.
2. Only one or two fingers should fit under the harness at the chest.
3. If you can pinch a fold of the strap at the shoulder, tighten it.
4. Blanket over the fastened harness, never under your baby.
5. Hats off once the car is warm.
Source: RoSPA, NHS and Lullaby Trust

D.topic: Parenting Tips: #60 Baby-proofing before they crawl

ig.text:
The best time to baby-proof is before your baby can move. Once they crawl, things happen fast.
Start on your hands and knees. That's their view of every room.
👉 Swipe for 6 jobs from NHS safety advice, including the hot drink fact most parents don't know.
📌 Save it and tick them off this weekend.
🔗 Compare safety gate prices from UK shops: link in bio.
#babyproofinguk #ukmums #newparentsuk #babysafetyuk #mumlifeuk

pin.text: Get down on the floor and look around: that's your baby's view. Fit stair gates to BS EN 1930:2011 at the top and bottom of the stairs, tie up blind cords, keep button batteries well away, keep hot drinks out of reach (they can scald 15 minutes later), fit window catches that open no more than 6.5cm, and keep medicines and laundry capsules out of reach and sight. Compare safety gate prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: NHS.

pinterestData.pinTitle: Baby-Proofing Before They Crawl: 6 Jobs to Do Now (UK)

descendants.text: Compare safety gate prices from UK shops https://babysorted.com/catalog

th.text:
Baby-proofing before they crawl, from NHS advice:
1. Stair gates at the top and bottom, until at least age 2.
2. Blind cords tied up and fixed out of reach.
3. Button batteries well away: swallowed, they can cause severe internal burns.
4. A hot drink can still scald 15 minutes after it's made.
5. Window catches that stop windows opening more than 6.5cm.
Source: NHS
Which job did you leave too late?

pin.text: Sterilise bottles and teats until your baby is at least 12 months old. Wash in hot soapy water first. Cold-water solution needs at least 30 minutes and a fresh batch every 24 hours. Boil for at least 10 minutes. A dishwasher cleans but doesn't sterilise. Out of the steriliser? Put teats and lids on straight away. Compare steriliser prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: NHS.
mediaAltText: Parent holding a baby's feet on a bed above six NHS rules for sterilising bottles with a white electric steriliser, on pink.

th.text:
How long should you sterilise bottles? The NHS says until your baby is at least 12 months.
1. Wash in hot soapy water first, then rinse.
2. Cold-water solution: at least 30 minutes, fresh every 24 hours.
3. Boiling: at least 10 minutes, everything under the water.
4. A dishwasher cleans but doesn't sterilise.
5. Taking bottles out? Put teats and lids on straight away.
Source: NHS
Which method do you use?

L2.topic: Lunch extra: winter walks without overheating (topics #37, #9)

pin.text: Never cover the pram with a blanket or cloth that stops air flowing. Take hats and hoods off indoors and in a warm car. Check the chest or back of the neck: sweaty or clammy means too hot, so take a layer off. Napping indoors? Outdoor clothes off, and no hot water bottles. Compare footmuff prices from UK shops at BabySorted. Source: The Lullaby Trust, the UK safer baby sleep charity.

th.text:
Wrapping up for a winter walk? Warm is good. Too warm isn't.
1. Never cover the pram with a blanket or cloth that stops the air flowing.
2. Hats and hoods off indoors and in a warm car.
3. Check the chest or back of the neck. Sweaty or clammy means too hot.
4. Napping when you get home? Take outdoor clothes off.
Source: Lullaby Trust
